author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The New Hampshire Fisher Cats were shut out 8-0 by the Harrisburg Senators on Thursday, even as the home pitching staff recorded 13 strikeouts. The result came during New Hampshire’s final homestand of the season at Delta Dental Stadium in Manchester.

The strikeout total was the clearest positive in a game controlled by Harrisburg. New Hampshire’s pitchers repeatedly generated swing-and-miss outs, but the Senators still built enough offense to separate. Without run support, every Harrisburg scoring inning carried added weight as the game moved along.

For the Fisher Cats, the final score underscored the difference between isolated pitching success and a complete team result. Strikeouts can limit balls in play and prevent runners from advancing, but they cannot offset walks, hits or defensive pressure when the lineup is unable to answer on the scoreboard.

The club’s closing homestand continues through the weekend, giving New Hampshire another opportunity to respond before the home schedule ends. The series also offers local fans a final look at the Double-A roster in Manchester, where individual development remains important even when the team result is one-sided.
dek: New Hampshire’s pitchers piled up strikeouts Thursday, while the offense was shut out in an 8-0 defeat during the final homestand.
headline: Fisher Cats strike out 13 but fall 8-0 to Harrisburg
